claims.statement: Talon's `make test` first runs WhatsApp bridge Node tests, then runs the selected `TEST_FILE` with non-Unix sockets disabled, Unix sockets allowed, a 10-second pytest timeout, and coverage; `make lint` runs Ruff checks/format diff and `ty` for Talon source.

Talon cron-expression tests protect calendar semantics including day-of-month/day-of-week matching, `L`/`LW`/`W`/last-weekday/nth-weekday extensions, leap-year and rare future matches, and rejection of expressions that can never fire.

Talon schedules preserve requested local wall-clock behavior across daylight-saving transitions: spring gaps snap forward without duplicate firing, fall-back ambiguous times fire once, and daily schedules retain their local hour including sub-hour gaps.

Before invoking a due job, `CronJobStore.advance_next_run` advances or disables the occurrence and persists the claimed record; this claim-before-run ordering prevents a due one-shot from remaining due while its callback runs.

`until` is valid only for recurring jobs and is inclusive for a due occurrence, with a five-minute grace for scheduler latency; a run missed beyond that grace is disabled rather than delivered after the requested window.
The scheduler records success, runner failures, and delivery failures after claiming a job, suppresses delivery for `[SILENT]` output, and continues scanning after an unexpected tick failure.

Finished or expired jobs are normally discarded on a later scheduler sweep, but failed final runs and jobs claimed without a recorded outcome are retained for inspection until retention pruning; a newly enabled replacement schedule prevents removal.

`open_checkpointer` defaults to Talon's local SQLite URI, selects either a built-in URI scheme or exactly one checkpoint-backend entry point, owns the selected async context lifecycle, and turns unexpected initialization failures into a credential-safe `TalonConfigError`.

Cron stores that address the same resolved jobs file share a reentrant in-process lock for complete storage mutations and reads, while job execution and delivery remain outside the lock and external processes are not coordinated.

Concurrent cron mutation tests cover same-instance and separate-store callers and show that a contested claim is exclusive, concurrent creation is retained through every mutation type, and readers observe completed persisted writes.

Talon pairing persists provider-scoped pending and approved senders with locked atomic replacement, rejects unsafe or invalid store state for admission, and uses expiring single-use codes that only an operator-facing approval surface can consume.

Slack pairing tests verify that unknown senders receive at most one code in their DM, unknown channel mentions only create a request after a DM can be opened, known senders do not trigger DM opening, and authorized `/talon pair` approval admits the sender without granting command access to an unauthorized coworker.

Slack OAuth-context tests exclude loopback OAuth callbacks from retrieved thread history before truncation and ensure unsolicited or historical callback text does not become model input or expose callback secrets in an agent request representation.

dcode's system-prompt smoke test composes a real CLI agent with real middleware and a fake chat model, fixes machine-dependent settings and paths, captures the first system message, and snapshots both interactive and headless prompt variants.
The dcode prompt tests separately verify that memory and secret-handling instructions remain present while interactive and headless modes expose different reachable interaction guidance.

SubagentPanel tests mount the real Textual widget with `run_test()` and assert observable selection, persistent collapse preference, reset/cancellation/replay behavior, hostile-label sanitization, responsive header rendering, and wall-clock phase duration.
The dcode Makefile provides network-restricted parallel unit tests and an explicit `update-snapshots` target that runs smoke snapshots with the `--update-snapshots` option.

The Deep Agents SDK unit-test target runs pytest in parallel with sockets disabled except Unix sockets, disables benchmarks, and collects coverage; its separate integration target uses a 30-second timeout.

Skills tests run synchronous and asynchronous agent invocation paths and show that a skill tool becomes bound only after a successful normalized `SKILL.md` read; calls before that disclosure or in the same turn are rejected without execution.
Skills disclosure is state-sensitive: compaction that drops the skill read withdraws the tool, and stale or incompatible checkpointed disclosure records do not authorize a later skill-tool call.

Skill-tool tests preserve capability precedence and isolation: registered or dynamically exposed tools win over same-named skill tools, while a declarative subagent receives only its explicitly configured skill tools.

On `ServerReady`, dcode settles connection state, installs the agent and MCP snapshot, removes transient startup-failure widgets, refreshes MCP state, and synchronizes the existing status bar model; it warns rather than silently leaving stale UI when the status bar or runtime model identity is missing.

ChatInput submission pauses allow only commands derived from `ALWAYS_IMMEDIATE | HIDDEN_COMMANDS` through the ordinary Enter path, while ordinary messages and other commands remain editable; blocked attempts preserve pasted text and image attachments.

The command registry marks `/install`, `/reload`, and `/update` as normally queue-bound startup-recovery commands; after a startup error they bypass the queue only with no active agent or shell work, while unrelated queued commands remain pending.

Status-bar model and effort picker hit testing is driven by metadata on rendered text spans, so mounted Textual tests locate painted cells and verify picker clicks do not bubble, focus recovery does not consume later clicks, and Ctrl-click copies the full model slug.

QuickJS subagent dispatch persists child cost receipts in checkpoint storage and transfers their settled total and breakdown to the parent, deduplicating receipt namespaces on replay; cost tests verify durable totals and complete breakdowns across fresh-runtime resume, interruption, cancellation, and failures.

The entire-thread cost formatter suppresses detail unless a version-one breakdown has complete history; otherwise it formats inclusive input/output rows and subsets, marks incomplete values and unpriceable requests as partial, and reports unattributed cost, while legacy dollar-only receipts remain chargeable but produce no table.
